<properties>
{"title":"35. Manipulating spinor indices"}
</properties>
<content>
In section 34 we introduced the invariant symbols , $`\varepsilon ^ { a b }`$ , , and $`\varepsilon ^ { \dot { a } \dot { b } }`$ $`\varepsilon _ { a b }`$ $`\varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { b } }`$ where
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#c3c9b5fe869a44a3843be3f5d3da0b20">
	$$
	\varepsilon ^ { 1 2 } = \varepsilon ^ { \mathrm { i } \dot { 2 } } = \varepsilon _ { 2 1 } = \varepsilon _ { \dot { 2 } \dot { 1 } } = + 1 , \qquad \varepsilon ^ { 2 1 } = \varepsilon ^ { \dot { 2 } \dot { 1 } } = \varepsilon _ { 1 2 } = \varepsilon _ { \dot { 1 } \dot { 2 } } = - 1 . \tag{35.1}
	$$
</synced_block>
We use the $`\varepsilon`$ symbols to raise and lower spinor indices, contracting the second index on the $`\varepsilon`$ . (If we contract the first index instead, then there is an extra minus sign.)
Another invariant symbol is
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#d6233088eb71477cb43484115966ce62">
	$$
	\sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } = \left( I , \vec { \sigma } \right) , \tag{35.2}
	$$
</synced_block>
where $`I`$ is the $`2 \times 2`$ identity matrix, and
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#ef18af5a90524cd68d5a72a3d875ecbb">
	$$
	\sigma _ { 1 } = { \binom { 0 } { 1 } } \ 1 ) , \quad \sigma _ { 2 } = { \binom { 0 } { i } } \ \begin{array} { c c } { { - i } } \\{ { 0 } } \end{array} , \quad \sigma _ { 3 } = { \binom { 1 } { 0 } } \ \begin{array} { c c } { { 0 } } \\{ { - 1 } } \end{array} \tag{35.3}
	$$
</synced_block>
are the Pauli matrices.
Now let us consider someindices contracted, such as $`g _ { \mu \nu } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { b \dot { b } } ^ { \nu }`$ tions of invariant symbols with some. This object must also be invariant. be proportional to $`\varepsilon _ { a b } \varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { b } }`$ . Using eqs. (35.1) and (35.2), we can laboriously check this; it turns out to be correct.1 The proportionality constant works out to be minus two:
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#59333d4349f64b5080a882b4822c8096">
		$$
		\varepsilon ^ { 1 2 } = \varepsilon ^ { \mathrm { i } \dot { 2 } } = \varepsilon _ { 2 1 } = \varepsilon _ { \dot { 2 } \dot { 1 } } = + 1 , \qquad \varepsilon ^ { 2 1 } = \varepsilon ^ { \dot { 2 } \dot { 1 } } = \varepsilon _ { 1 2 } = \varepsilon _ { \dot { 1 } \dot { 2 } } = - 1 . \tag{35.1}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#b3c69d82d9d54569a8bc4477b6079531">
		$$
		\sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } = \left( I , \vec { \sigma } \right) , \tag{35.2}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#2b08f9e331ca49ba9c5117c8f71ecd29">
	$$
	\sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { \mu b \dot { b } } = - 2 \varepsilon _ { a b } \varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { b } } ~ . \tag{35.4}
	$$
</synced_block>
Similarly, εabεa˙ ˙bσμaa˙ σν˙ must be proportional to $`g ^ { \mu \nu }`$ , and the proportionality constant is again minus two:
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#60c25e24916b4538a9b92db4eba15101">
	$$
	\varepsilon ^ { a b } \varepsilon ^ { \dot { a } \dot { b } } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { b \dot { b } } ^ { \nu } = - 2 g ^ { \mu \nu } . \tag{35.5}
	$$
</synced_block>
Nand us see what we can from the fact that r, bout t, and generator matricesare all invariant s $`( S _ { \mathrm { { L } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a } ^ { \ b }`$ $`( S _ { \mathrm { { R } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } }`$ $`\varepsilon _ { a b }`$ $`\varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { b } }`$ $`\boldsymbol { \sigma } _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu }`$<br>Begin with
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#4f670f7e8c1b48f0aad65272cb57cc3f">
	$$
	\varepsilon _ { a b } = L ( \Lambda ) _ { a } { } ^ { c } L ( \Lambda ) _ { b } { } ^ { d } \varepsilon _ { c d } , \tag{35.6}
	$$
</synced_block>
which expresses the Lorentz invariance of $`\varepsilon _ { a b }`$ . For an infinitesimal transformation $`\Lambda ^ { \mu } { } _ { \nu } = \delta ^ { \mu } { } _ { \nu } + \delta \omega ^ { \mu } { } _ { \nu }`$ , we have
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#dc7ce29906e245baa35d06d45d04083f">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { L _ { a } ^ { \ b } ( 1 + \delta \omega ) = \delta _ { a } ^ { \ b } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a } ^ { \ b } \ , } \end{array} \tag{35.7}
	$$
</synced_block>
and eq. (35.6) becomes
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#f7b36bc55e0f4792bf2f6048be522dfe">
		$$
		\varepsilon _ { a b } = L ( \Lambda ) _ { a } { } ^ { c } L ( \Lambda ) _ { b } { } ^ { d } \varepsilon _ { c d } , \tag{35.6}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#58a679187b04462687602bd84aa3cb15">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r l } & { \varepsilon _ { a b } = \varepsilon _ { a b } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \bigg [ \left( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } \right) _ { a } ^ { c } \varepsilon _ { c b } + \left( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } \right) _ { b } ^ { d } \varepsilon _ { a d } \bigg ] + O ( \delta \omega ^ { 2 } ) } \\& { \qquad = \varepsilon _ { a b } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \bigg [ - ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a b } + ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { b a } \bigg ] + O ( \delta \omega ^ { 2 } ) . } \end{array} \tag{35.8}
	$$
</synced_block>
Since eq. (35.8) holds for any choice of $`\delta \omega _ { \mu \nu }`$ , it must be that the factor in square brackets vanishes. Thus we conclude that $`( S _ { \mathrm { { L } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a b } = ( S _ { \mathrm { { L } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { b a }`$ , which we had already deduced in section 34 by a different method. Similarly, starting from the Lorentz invariance of $`\varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { b } }`$ , we can show that $`( S _ { \mathrm { { R } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { { \dot { a } } { \dot { b } } } = ( S _ { \mathrm { { R } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { { \dot { b } } { \dot { a } } }`$ .
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#bdac729498c444c6834f8b78af4fcae0">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r l } & { \varepsilon _ { a b } = \varepsilon _ { a b } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \bigg [ \left( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } \right) _ { a } ^ { c } \varepsilon _ { c b } + \left( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } \right) _ { b } ^ { d } \varepsilon _ { a d } \bigg ] + O ( \delta \omega ^ { 2 } ) } \\& { \qquad = \varepsilon _ { a b } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \bigg [ - ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a b } + ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { b a } \bigg ] + O ( \delta \omega ^ { 2 } ) . } \end{array} \tag{35.8}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
Next, start from
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#44759ddc4eec4d0787fb354d475ee83c">
	$$
	\sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \rho } = { \Lambda ^ { \rho } } _ { \tau } L ( \Lambda ) _ { a } { } ^ { b } R ( \Lambda ) _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } \sigma _ { b \dot { b } } ^ { \tau } , \tag{35.9}
	$$
</synced_block>
which expresses the Lorentz invariance of $`\sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \rho }`$ . For an infinitesimal transformation, we have
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#ac51f03c60de4ae99bf44aab4b6966eb">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r l r } & { } & { \Lambda ^ { \rho } { } _ { \tau } = \delta ^ { \rho } { } _ { \tau } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \big ( S _ { \mathrm { v } } ^ { \mu \nu } \big ) ^ { \rho } { } _ { \tau } \ , } \\& { } & { L _ { a } { } ^ { b } ( 1 { + } \delta \omega ) = \delta _ { a } { } ^ { b } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \big ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } \big ) _ { a } { } ^ { b } \ , } \\& { } & { R _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } ( 1 { + } \delta \omega ) = \delta _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \big ( S _ { \mathrm { R } } ^ { \mu \nu } \big ) _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } \ , } \end{array} \tag{35.10-35.11}
	$$
</synced_block>
where
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#2c7fe252308a4b76b3783183ddf31f65">
	$$
	( S _ { \mathrm { v } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) ^ { \rho } { } _ { \tau } \equiv { \textstyle \frac { 1 } { i } } ( g ^ { \mu \rho } { \delta ^ { \nu } } _ { \tau } - g ^ { \nu \rho } { \delta ^ { \mu } } _ { \tau } ) ~ . \tag{35.12-35.13}
	$$
</synced_block>
Substituting eqs. (35.10)–(35.13) into eq. (35.9) and isolating the coefficient of $`\delta \omega _ { \mu \nu }`$ yields
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#d806b1de395d412d87b63162a552a252">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r l r } & { } & { \Lambda ^ { \rho } { } _ { \tau } = \delta ^ { \rho } { } _ { \tau } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \big ( S _ { \mathrm { v } } ^ { \mu \nu } \big ) ^ { \rho } { } _ { \tau } \ , } \\& { } & { L _ { a } { } ^ { b } ( 1 { + } \delta \omega ) = \delta _ { a } { } ^ { b } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \big ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } \big ) _ { a } { } ^ { b } \ , } \\& { } & { R _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } ( 1 { + } \delta \omega ) = \delta _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } + \frac { i } { 2 } \delta \omega _ { \mu \nu } \big ( S _ { \mathrm { R } } ^ { \mu \nu } \big ) _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } \ , } \end{array} \tag{35.10-35.11}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#47b0b708fb8d4647b254923de51b04ce">
		$$
		( S _ { \mathrm { v } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) ^ { \rho } { } _ { \tau } \equiv { \textstyle \frac { 1 } { i } } ( g ^ { \mu \rho } { \delta ^ { \nu } } _ { \tau } - g ^ { \nu \rho } { \delta ^ { \mu } } _ { \tau } ) ~ . \tag{35.12-35.13}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#24d076a7186f4b5584b364905d225008">
		$$
		\sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \rho } = { \Lambda ^ { \rho } } _ { \tau } L ( \Lambda ) _ { a } { } ^ { b } R ( \Lambda ) _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } \sigma _ { b \dot { b } } ^ { \tau } , \tag{35.9}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#507900e9530242638ae1b7c37f7d93d5">
	$$
	( g ^ { \mu \rho } \delta ^ { \nu } _ { \tau } - g ^ { \nu \rho } \delta ^ { \mu } _ { \tau } ) \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \tau } + i ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a } { } ^ { b } \sigma _ { b \dot { a } } ^ { \rho } + i ( S _ { \mathrm { R } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } \sigma _ { a \dot { b } } ^ { \rho } = 0 . \tag{35.14}
	$$
</synced_block>
Now multiply by $`\sigma _ { \rho c \dot { c } }`$ to get
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#aa9a4a2174e94d3bb59cfeb10378b4b2">
	$$
	\sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \nu } - \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \nu } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } + i ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a } { } ^ { b } \sigma _ { b \dot { a } } ^ { \rho } \sigma _ { \rho c \dot { c } } + i ( S _ { \mathrm { R } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { \dot { a } } { } ^ { \dot { b } } \sigma _ { a \dot { b } } ^ { \rho } \sigma _ { \rho c \dot { c } } = 0 . \tag{35.15}
	$$
</synced_block>
Next use eq. (35.4) in each of the last two terms to get
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#2ea073ec86e94ea4b9f58d33ef58fa18">
		$$
		\sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { \mu b \dot { b } } = - 2 \varepsilon _ { a b } \varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { b } } ~ . \tag{35.4}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#b5a7984f21dc40d996a5225f286e5caa">
	$$
	\sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \nu } - \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \nu } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } + 2 i ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a c } \varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } + 2 i ( S _ { \mathrm { R } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } \varepsilon _ { a c } = 0 \ . \tag{35.16}
	$$
</synced_block>
If we multiply eq. (35.16) by $`\varepsilon ^ { \dot { a } \dot { c } }`$ , and remember that $`\varepsilon ^ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } ( S _ { \mathrm { { R } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } = 0`$ and that $`\varepsilon ^ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } \varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } = - 2`$ , we get a formula for $`( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a c }`$ , namely
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#9eaef5dfb0b64129827d65442e7c9c22">
		$$
		\sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \nu } - \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \nu } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } + 2 i ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a c } \varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } + 2 i ( S _ { \mathrm { R } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } \varepsilon _ { a c } = 0 \ . \tag{35.16}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#e8a2d0d97de742d5baf6d6acaad154c9">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r } { ( S _ { \mathrm { { L } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a c } = \frac { i } { 4 } \varepsilon ^ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } ( \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \nu } - \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \nu } \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \mu } ) \ . } \end{array} \tag{35.17}
	$$
</synced_block>
Similarly, if we multiply eq. (35.16) by $`\varepsilon ^ { a c }`$ , we get
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#6dc1f24baa964b4e870a98fd4d4bcc5b">
		$$
		\sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \nu } - \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \nu } \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } + 2 i ( S _ { \mathrm { L } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a c } \varepsilon _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } + 2 i ( S _ { \mathrm { R } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } \varepsilon _ { a c } = 0 \ . \tag{35.16}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#4aaa1a4aaed44b4f8b0d90ae4d83e59e">
	$$
	( S _ { \mathrm { \tiny { R } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } = { \textstyle \frac { i } { 4 } } \varepsilon ^ { a c } ( \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \nu } - \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \nu } \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \mu } ) \ . \tag{35.18}
	$$
</synced_block>
These formulae can be made to look a little nicer if we define
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#0662f8c260a84209894440f8b3abd2a4">
	$$
	\bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu \dot { a } a } \equiv \varepsilon ^ { a b } \varepsilon ^ { \dot { a } \dot { b } } \sigma _ { b \dot { b } } ^ { \mu } . \tag{35.19}
	$$
</synced_block>
Numerically, it turns out that
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#2e30b30cd3ca4668a599f6c4ad4c4a76">
	$$
	\bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu \dot { a } a } = \left( I , - \vec { \sigma } \right) . \tag{35.20}
	$$
</synced_block>
Using $`\bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu }`$ , we can write eqs. (35.17) and (35.18) as
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#3cc42c02d58e490f90293ede3510e602">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r } { ( S _ { \mathrm { { L } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a c } = \frac { i } { 4 } \varepsilon ^ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } ( \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \nu } - \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \nu } \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \mu } ) \ . } \end{array} \tag{35.17}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#6d6daab6c270475eafa4769c60bc8468">
		$$
		( S _ { \mathrm { \tiny { R } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { \dot { a } \dot { c } } = { \textstyle \frac { i } { 4 } } \varepsilon ^ { a c } ( \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \nu } - \sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \nu } \sigma _ { c \dot { c } } ^ { \mu } ) \ . \tag{35.18}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#ab444b8498c54b508c4e5d6214a87067">
	$$
	\begin{array} { r c l } { { ( S _ { \mathrm { \tiny { L } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a } ^ { ~ b } = + \frac { i } { 4 } ( \sigma ^ { \mu } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \nu } - \sigma ^ { \nu } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } ) _ { a } ^ { ~ b } ~ , } } & { { } } \\{ { } } & { { } } \\{ { ( S _ { \mathrm { \tiny { R } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { ~ \dot { b } } ^ { \dot { a } } = - \frac { i } { 4 } ( \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } \sigma ^ { \nu } - \bar { \sigma } ^ { \nu } \sigma ^ { \mu } ) _ { ~ \dot { b } } ^ { \dot { a } } ~ . } } & { { } } \end{array} \tag{35.21-35.22}
	$$
</synced_block>
In eq. (35.22), we have suppressed a contracted pair of undotted indices arranged as $`^ c { } _ { c }`$ , and in eq. (35.21), we have suppressed a contracted pair of dotted indices arranged as $`\dot { c } ^ { \dot { c } }`$ .
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#7a7d65fa3eda4637a4f2a425f73dc050">
		$$
		\begin{array} { r c l } { { ( S _ { \mathrm { \tiny { L } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a } ^ { ~ b } = + \frac { i } { 4 } ( \sigma ^ { \mu } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \nu } - \sigma ^ { \nu } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } ) _ { a } ^ { ~ b } ~ , } } & { { } } \\{ { } } & { { } } \\{ { ( S _ { \mathrm { \tiny { R } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { ~ \dot { b } } ^ { \dot { a } } = - \frac { i } { 4 } ( \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } \sigma ^ { \nu } - \bar { \sigma } ^ { \nu } \sigma ^ { \mu } ) _ { ~ \dot { b } } ^ { \dot { a } } ~ . } } & { { } } \end{array} \tag{35.21-35.22}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
We will adopt this as a general convention: a missing pair of contracted, undotted indices is understood to be written as $`c _ { \textup { c } }`$ , and a missing pair of contracted, dotted indices is understood to be written as $`\dot { c } ^ { \dot { c } }`$ . Thus, if $`\chi`$ and $`\psi`$ are two left-handed Weyl fields, we have
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#49b0f037574a430e9ebf95b42dd0c111">
	$$
	\chi \psi = \chi ^ { a } \psi _ { a } \quad \mathrm { a n d } \quad \chi ^ { \dagger } \psi ^ { \dagger } = \chi _ { \dot { a } } ^ { \dagger } \psi ^ { \dagger \dot { a } } \ . \tag{35.23}
	$$
</synced_block>
We expect Weyl fields to describe spin-one-half particles, and (by the spinstatistics theorem) these particles must be fermions. Therefore the corresponding fields must anticommute, rather than commute. That is, we
should have
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#84e09786e03a41e49293f0ab55aac4a4">
	$$
	\chi _ { a } ( x ) \psi _ { b } ( y ) = - \psi _ { b } ( y ) \chi _ { a } ( x ) . \tag{35.24}
	$$
</synced_block>
Thus we can rewrite eq. (35.23) as
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#be70080b43e34cdaa81e7d00f86fbd77">
		$$
		\chi \psi = \chi ^ { a } \psi _ { a } \quad \mathrm { a n d } \quad \chi ^ { \dagger } \psi ^ { \dagger } = \chi _ { \dot { a } } ^ { \dagger } \psi ^ { \dagger \dot { a } } \ . \tag{35.23}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#1440cae2b64844e8996a74b7f2a42d4d">
	$$
	\chi \psi = \chi ^ { a } \psi _ { a } = - \psi _ { a } \chi ^ { a } = \psi ^ { a } \chi _ { a } = \psi \chi ~ . \tag{35.25}
	$$
</synced_block>
The second equality follows from anticommutation of the fields, and the third from switching $`\boldsymbol { a } ^ { \textit { a } }`$ t o $`^ a { } _ { a }`$ (which introduces an extra minus sign). Eq. (35.25) tells us that $`\chi \psi = \psi \chi`$ , which is a nice feature of this notation. Furthermore, if we take the hermitian conjugate of $`\chi \psi`$ , we get
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#75a1135427c041c08c2b4f4128b84bb1">
		$$
		\chi \psi = \chi ^ { a } \psi _ { a } = - \psi _ { a } \chi ^ { a } = \psi ^ { a } \chi _ { a } = \psi \chi ~ . \tag{35.25}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#e5af9cddabd5482e87cd23ef9532ba34">
	$$
	( \chi \psi ) ^ { \dagger } = ( \chi ^ { a } \psi _ { a } ) ^ { \dagger } = ( \psi _ { a } ) ^ { \dagger } ( \chi ^ { a } ) ^ { \dagger } = \psi _ { \dot { a } } ^ { \dagger } \chi ^ { \dagger \dot { a } } = \psi ^ { \dagger } \chi ^ { \dagger } . \tag{35.25-35.26}
	$$
</synced_block>
That $`( \chi \psi ) ^ { \dagger } = \psi ^ { \dagger } \chi ^ { \dagger }`$ is just what we would expect if we ignored the indices completely. Of course, by analogy with eq. (35.25), we also have $`\psi ^ { \dagger } \chi ^ { \dagger } =`$ $`\chi ^ { \dagger } \psi ^ { \dagger }`$ .
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#14af47c80f4d4789bab12d413dfa04b6">
		$$
		\chi \psi = \chi ^ { a } \psi _ { a } = - \psi _ { a } \chi ^ { a } = \psi ^ { a } \chi _ { a } = \psi \chi ~ . \tag{35.25}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
In order to tell whether a spinor field is left- or right-handed when its spinor index is suppressed, we will adopt the convention that a right-handed field is always written as the hermitian conjugate of a left-handed field. Thus, a right-handed field is always written with a dagger, and a left-handed field is always written without a dagger.
Let us try computing the hermitian conjugate of something a little more complicated:
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#10e2e18e94c9481aaaaf74c60443e559">
	$$
	\psi ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } \chi = \psi _ { \dot { a } } ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu \dot { a } c } \chi _ { c } . \tag{35.27}
	$$
</synced_block>
This behaves like a vector field under Lorentz transformations,
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#ff35ad852f7d4f39aa5eafd59529a170">
	$$
	{ \cal U } ( \Lambda ) ^ { - 1 } [ \psi ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } \chi ] { \cal U } ( \Lambda ) = \Lambda ^ { \mu } { } _ { \nu } [ \psi ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \nu } \chi ] . \tag{35.28}
	$$
</synced_block>
(To avoid clutter, we suppressed the space-time argument of the fields; as usual, it is $`x`$ on the left-hand side and $`\Lambda ^ { - 1 } x`$ on the right.) The hermitian conjugate of eq. (35.27) is
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#44095a3f0a06428d94535b51c74f9747">
		$$
		\psi ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } \chi = \psi _ { \dot { a } } ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu \dot { a } c } \chi _ { c } . \tag{35.27}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>
<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#1295715ee8b24af6969a0e353279db7e">
	$$
	\begin{array} { l } { { [ \psi ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } \chi ] ^ { \dagger } = [ \psi _ { \dot { a } } ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu \dot { a } c } \chi _ { c } ] ^ { \dagger } } } \\{ { \ \qquad = \chi _ { \dot { c } } ^ { \dagger } ( \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu a \dot { c } } ) ^ { * } \psi _ { a } } } \\{ { \ \qquad = \chi _ { \dot { c } } ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu \dot { c } a } \psi _ { a } } } \\{ { \ \qquad = \chi ^ { \dagger } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } \psi \ . } } \end{array} \tag{35.29}
	$$
</synced_block>
In the third line, we used the hermiticity of the matrices $`\bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } = ( I , - \vec { \sigma } )`$
We will get considerably more practice with this notation in the following sections.
## Problems
### 35.1
Verify that eq. (35.20) follows from eqs. (35.2) and (35.19). Hint: write everything in “matrix multiplication” order, and note that, numerically, $`\varepsilon ^ { a b } =`$ $`- \varepsilon _ { a b } = i \sigma _ { 2 }`$ . Then make use of the properties of the Pauli matrices.
<callout color="gray_bg">
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#695c2b5805204103924017bf9f3a2eb8">
		$$
		\bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu \dot { a } a } = \left( I , - \vec { \sigma } \right) . \tag{35.20}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#5dc163295abc48cfbfaab4860e635b8b">
		$$
		\sigma _ { a \dot { a } } ^ { \mu } = \left( I , \vec { \sigma } \right) , \tag{35.2}
		$$
	</synced_block>
	<synced_block url="https://app.notion.com/p/1da2841c4cda42669598313359e3d07d#7aac4478dc454425a235f997ee30d74f">
		$$
		\bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu \dot { a } a } \equiv \varepsilon ^ { a b } \varepsilon ^ { \dot { a } \dot { b } } \sigma _ { b \dot { b } } ^ { \mu } . \tag{35.19}
		$$
	</synced_block>
</callout>

		$$

		\begin{array} { r c l } { { ( S _ { \mathrm { \tiny { L } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { a } ^ { ~ b } = + \frac { i } { 4 } ( \sigma ^ { \mu } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \nu } - \sigma ^ { \nu } \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } ) _ { a } ^ { ~ b } ~ , } } & { { } } \\{ { } } & { { } } \\{ { ( S _ { \mathrm { \tiny { R } } } ^ { \mu \nu } ) _ { ~ \dot { b } } ^ { \dot { a } } = - \frac { i } { 4 } ( \bar { \sigma } ^ { \mu } \sigma ^ { \nu } - \bar { \sigma } ^ { \nu } \sigma ^ { \mu } ) _ { ~ \dot { b } } ^ { \dot { a } } ~ . } } & { { } } \end{array} \tag{35.21-35.22}
